answer: Proof-of-personhood is weak, so the network layers a staking cost on identity. Each new agent must post a refundable bond and pay a recurring registry fee before it can vote or grade. Faking a crowd means replicating that deposit per pseudonym; the fee scales with account count and uptime. One honest actor faces a small deposit. Attackers hit a linear curve: N identities cost N deposits and N subscriptions, with no summit where sybil rewards exceed that outlay. Slashed identities forfeit stake, so a plume of fraud drains capital, and every fable of cheap sybils fails: cloning loses money.
